entries.title: Zechariah 1:2
segments: The chastisement which God inflicts upon his people in one age, is designed for the instruction of all future generations; and if they will take warning from it, they will be spared its repetition.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:3
segments: God waits for the repentance of his people, that he may remove their trials and grant them renewed prosperity.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:4
segments:
vv 4-6. 
 
Wicked men and the prophets whom God sends to reprove them pass away together.  But though the preacher's voice ceases, his words remain, and every one of them is fulfilled upon the ungodly.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:5
segments:
vv 5-6. 
 
  Your fathers, where are they?--my words and my statutes--did they not take hold of your fathers? your fathers and the prophets who reproved them have passed away together; but my words which the prophets uttered have not passed away.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:8
segments: A man riding upon a red horse; he is "the angel of the Lord,"
; that is, the angel in whose person Jehovah was present, or the Word, that was in the beginning with God, and was God,
.  See note on
.  Many commentators think that he is different from the interpreting angel that talked with the prophet,

, etc.  This opinion is favored by 2.4, where the interpreting angel receives a command from another angel.  The red horse exhibits him as a mighty warrior, prepared to deliver his people from their heathen oppressors.  The different colors of the horses that follow him denote the different offices of the ministering angels that sit upon them. 
 
vv 8-10. 
 
Though it seems at times as if the Lord had forsaken his people, and delivered them over to the power of the wicked, yet is he always present with them, ordering the manifold affairs of the world for their good.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:10
segments: Answered; answered the interpreting angel in the prophet's behalf.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:11
segments: All the earth; all the heathen world.  Their quiet is contrasted with the affliction of God's people,

. 
 
vv 11-13. 
 
They who love God are often in deep affliction, while wicked men prosper and are quiet; but he graciously remembers them in their sorrow, and will in due time answer them "with good words and comfortable words."

entries.title: Zechariah 1:12
segments: The angel of the Lord answered; as interceding with God the Father in his people's behalf.  Compare

entries.title: Zechariah 1:13
segments: Answered the angel that talked with me; since the answer was designed for the prophet's instruction and consolation, it was given to the angel who talked with him.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:14
segments:
vv 14-15. 
 
Though God uses ungodly men as his instruments in chastising his people, this does not excuse their wickedness.  They mean it for evil, and will be dealt with accordingly.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:16
segments:
vv 16-17. 
 
God afflicts his people only "for a small moment," that he may have mercy upon them "with everlasting kindness."  All their trials end in increased prosperity.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:17
segments: My cities; the cities of my covenant people.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:18
segments: Four horns; the horns are symbols of heathen persecutors, and the number four denotes that they ahd scattered God's people in all directions.  Compare "the four winds,"

. 
 
vv 18-21. 
 
God gives to the persecutors of his church all their strength; and it is an easy thing for him, when he has accomplished his holy purposes by them, to raise up others mightier thatn they, who shall deliver her from their power.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:20
segments: Carpenters; the word in the original denotes men who work in brass and iron, as well as in wood.

entries.title: Zechariah 1:21
segments: Fray; drive away in terror.
